land.text: Nyasaland, the British protectorate (the former British Central Africa Protectorate)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws Nyasaland inside its 'British East Africa' shape (1961-1968), which the british-east-africa dossier closes for Malawi at 6 July 1964.

capitals.name: Zomba
capitals.note: Nyasaland infobox 'Capital: Zomba'. Coordinates from the gazetteer (Natural Earth). The Lilongwe page: Lilongwe 'became the capital of Malawi in 1975, replacing the previous capital, Zomba'.

capitals.name: Lilongwe
capitals.note: 'The first plan for Lilongwe was published in 1955, before the decision was made in 1965 to move the capital from Zomba to Lilongwe.' 'The last government offices were relocated to Lilongwe in 2005.' Coordinates as given on the Lilongwe page.

correction.text: Nyasaland within its frontiers, independent as Malawi on 6 July 1964 (a republic from 6 July 1966): the same land as the 1967 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins 1967 against 'on 6 July 1964, Nyasaland became independent from British rule and renamed itself Malawi'. The land lies inside Cliopatria's British East Africa shape until 1968; that overlap is for the british-east-africa dossier to resolve.

92,918 km2 for 1967-1975 against the infobox 'Total: 118,484 km2' with 'Water (%): 20.6%'. Land alone is about 94,100 km2 (118,484 x 0.794), so the shape matches the land (ratio 0.99); against the total the ratio is 0.78, inside the factor of two. The gazetteer shows the shape excludes Lake Malawi: 309 cells against 401 for modern Malawi. The Nyasaland infobox gives 102,564 km2 for the colony. The row's listed modern countries (Zambia, Mozambique) are overlap of cells along the frontier.
93,031 km2 for 1976-2023, 113 km2 (0.1%) above the earlier shape. The page records no border change and says nothing of Zomba or the 1975 move; shape refinement, no ledger event.

ledger.note: 6 July 1964: Nyasaland becomes independent as Malawi under Hastings Banda. 'on 6 July 1964, Nyasaland became independent from British rule and renamed itself Malawi'; infobox 'Declared: 6 July 1964'. Nyasaland page: it had been in the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland from 1 August 1953, 'formally dissolved on 31 December 1963', and reached internal self-government in February 1963.

6 July 1966: Malawi becomes a republic with Banda as president. 'Under a new constitution, Malawi became a republic in 1966 with Banda as its first president' (infobox 'Republic: 6 July 1966'); Nyasaland page: 'the country became the Republic of Malawi, a republic within the Commonwealth, on 6 July 1966'. No land changes; colour continues.

1975: the capital moves from Zomba to Lilongwe. 'Lilongwe became the capital of Malawi in 1975, replacing the previous capital, Zomba'; the decision was taken in 1965 and 'The last government offices were relocated to Lilongwe in 2005'.

certainty.note: Neither page opened gives a boundary treaty or survey: the Malawi page only says it is 'bordered by Zambia to the northwest, Tanzania to the northeast, and Mozambique to the south, southwest, and east', and no page records a frontier change after 1964, so the colonial frontier is taken to have carried over. The lake frontier is not described by either page and the shape leaves Lake Malawi out.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Malawi' begins 1967 against independence on 6 July 1964, so a 1964-1966 keyframe is added; it overlaps British East Africa (1961-1968) in 1967-1968. The Malawi page is silent on any lake boundary with Tanzania or Mozambique ('The page does not mention a Lake Malawi/Lake Nyasa boundary dispute'), on Zomba and on the capital move; those facts come from the Lilongwe and Nyasaland pages. The only territorial remark on the Malawi page is 'disputes over the use of the Zambezi River' with Mozambique, which it presents as not territorial. The Malawi page gives the constitution as 18 May 1994 in the infobox and 18 May 1995 in the text. The 1994 multiparty election ('Banda was defeated by Bakili Muluzi') moved no land. No war found on the pages opened, hence wars is empty. Rulers omitted. Page budget: two pages plus the Lilongwe page for the capital. native_names left empty: no page read gives one.
